name: The test people
land: A river mouth with reed beds.

myths.title: The first net
myths.text: Before the people there was only water. The heron stood in it and waited. A woman came and asked for a fish, and the heron gave her one and then another, and asked for nothing. So she wove a net and fed the heron first.

myths.title: The empty season
myths.text: One year the people ate before the heron. The fish went deep and did not return until the eldest stood in the water for a day and a night.

entries.statement: The heron stands for the dead, who gave before they were asked.
The first fish of every catch is given to the heron before anyone eats.
In a bad season the eldest must stand in the water for a day and a night.
Nets are hung on the north side of every house.

customs.name: Feeding the heron
customs.visible: At dusk someone carries the first fish to the post and leaves it there.

villagers.name: Maëlle
villagers.slant: She tells the first story as a story about patience.

lines.refusal: That is for the shaman to say.
lines.withholding: That is not for a stranger.

villagers.name: Old Tam

knowsMyths.version: One year we ate first, and the fish left. That is all I was told.

villagers.slant: He thinks the empty season was only bad weather.

silences: What is done when a heron dies.
